conditions.requires: JEM Races client support checks during multiplayer connection transitions

change.summary: Use one stable ClientPacketListener snapshot when checking whether the JEM Races channel is available

modifiers.before: Always-active client paths checked Minecraft.getConnection and then fetched it again before reading the underlying network connection
modifiers.after: Each support check captures one ClientPacketListener snapshot, rejects null and uses the same snapshot for the underlying Forge channel check
modifiers.notes: Only lifecycle admission changes. Race state, packets, server authority and presentation remain unchanged

rationale.purpose: Prevent a valid multiplayer login or disconnect transition from turning a repeated global connection lookup into a client-side NullPointerException
rationale.decision_source: The user reproduced the production disconnect on 2026-10-31 after JEM Security 1.0.5 was installed. The displayed mapped exception and installed JEM Races bytecode identify the repeated Minecraft.getConnection lookup. The user explicitly required that bootstrap remain unchanged

introduced.summary: Capture and reuse one client connection snapshot in JEM Races support checks

history.summary: Repair the repeated production login disconnect without changing bootstrap or the race protocol

relations: Minecraft ClientPacketListener snapshot -> underlying Connection -> JEM Races Forge channel availability
notes: Five Whys: login disconnected -> a ClientPacketListener method was invoked on a null second lookup -> JEM Races queried the global connection twice -> the connection transition could invalidate the second value -> the support contract lacked a stable per-call snapshot
No registry identity, gameplay value, packet payload, server authority, JEM Security rule or bootstrap behavior changes
unresolved: Player acceptance on MineRENT remains pending
